reviewer.name: Claude Sonnet, fresh subagent (cold reader 2)
reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-26 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session)

evidence: Read the whole 'How to use this very large guide' paragraph with the draft in it, then the draft, then SOURCE. Draft judged: 'Also read some of the stuff in the daily and weekly sections, to make the practice your own.' It occurs once in CONTEXT, word for word. the_change names three moves and all three are there: 'look at the daily and weekly sections' became 'read some of the stuff in the daily and weekly sections'; the ending 'to make the practice your own' is kept; 'You can also' became 'Also'. One unlisted delta: a comma before 'to make...'. It changes no meaning and it matches the comma-before-purpose in the sentence just before ('...section, for the part of the practice no recording can decide in advance'), so I do not count it against the draft. Meaning: SOURCE gives 'You can also look at the daily and weekly sections to make the practice your own' (published guide: the sections help you make the practice your own). The draft keeps the same two sections and the same purpose and adds no fact, name or claim. There are two small shifts of force, neither a new claim. 'some of the stuff' narrows 'look at' to dipping in, which is the paragraph's own frame (it opens 'To make it easier, you can begin with...' and is all selective routes through a very large guide). Dropping 'You can' turns the permission into an imperative, but 'Also read' hangs off the preceding 'you can read the Let the next response guide you section', so it continues an optional list rather than issuing a requirement. Seam and voice: I felt no seam. 'read' repeats the verb of the sentence before, which is what makes the bare 'Also' natural; 'stuff' sits with the paragraph's existing 'lots of appendices... lots of topics', so the register there is already that loose; there is no tidy summary, hedge or moral he would not write. Tell rows: I answered all of T01-T29 and C01-C04 against the literal sentence in its context and find none actually happening. The ones I weighed: T02/T11/T13 (the paragraph is a roadmap, each sentence a signpost joined by 'then', 'Then,', 'Also') - that cadence is the job of a 'how to use this guide' paragraph, the swap adds no step and no bridge, and the paragraph still carries reasons ('for the part of the practice no recording can decide in advance', 'to make the practice your own'); T07 and T15 ('some of the stuff' is a humanizing tool's colloquial swap) - it carries meaning (a quantity and a generic reference to what the sections hold), is not a staged hesitation between engineered beats, and the rest of the sentence is the approved wording, so no AI structure is being camouflaged; T22 - the linter's 'You can also' coach register is gone and what remains is an instruction with its reason, not reassurance; T26 - 'read' twice in adjacent sentences and 'the practice' twice, neither distinctive and the first doing the parallel; C01-C04 - no inner child, no first-person fact, no named-entity claim, and 'the daily and weekly sections' are sections the guide itself has. Linter: the only finding, 'D9 follows the source order', is not a real problem here. This is a one-sentence swap into an unchanged paragraph, so it follows the replaced sentence's point by construction, and the order of that paragraph is the reading order it exists to give; the sentence still carries a reason clause, and I found neither T13 nor T09 in it. Accepted and listed in resolved_lint_labels.
